details:
I primarily play VRChat on a standalone Quest 3, and I'd like to request support for SpaceWarp (SSW).

The Quest 3 is capable of running VRChat reasonably well, but in many populated worlds and demanding situations the game typically runs at around 40–45 FPS. While this is playable, VR is extremely sensitive to frame rate, and smooth head movement is essential for comfort and immersion.

This is exactly the kind of scenario where SpaceWarp could make a significant difference.

Many standalone Quest games already use SSW to generate intermediate frames, allowing the experience to feel much smoother even when the game itself cannot render at the full display refresh rate. For VRChat, this could dramatically improve the standalone experience by effectively bringing motion much closer to the target refresh rate.

Benefits could include:

Significantly smoother head movement.

A much more comfortable experience in populated worlds.

Better frame pacing without requiring more powerful hardware.

A substantial quality-of-life improvement for standalone Quest users.

I understand there may be technical challenges or engine limitations, but I'd love to know:

Has the team considered implementing SpaceWarp for standalone Quest? If not, are there technical reasons that make it impractical?

I believe this feature could significantly improve the standalone VRChat experience for a large number of Quest users, especially on Quest 3.

If anyone else would like to see this feature, please consider upvoting this request so the developers know there is interest from the community.
title: Feature Request: Support  Application SpaceWarp (AppSW) on Standalone Quest
